label: Local authority
quiz: What did Lapulapu refuse to recognize in the dispute?

The fact that trading communities existed
The need to distinguish accounts from art
The location of the Pacific Ocean
retry: Why should a report distinguish Lapulapu from Zula?
They were local leaders who took different positions
They were two names for a single recorded decision
Both spoke for every island in the archipelago
Their choices prove every community agreed
hard: A student says Humabon's agreement settled Mactan's choice. What is the strongest correction?
An agreement by one leader does not establish another leader's consent
Nearby communities always make identical decisions
A foreign demand proves it was freely accepted
Trading with visitors transfers authority automatically

label: Causes of conflict
quiz: Which action shows coercion rather than a freely accepted agreement?
Using threats or force to demand obedience
Asking what another person thinks without threatening them
Comparing two historical sources
Choosing to exchange goods by agreement
retry: Which explanation connects the demands with the conflict?
Refusal met an attempt to impose authority by force
All leaders agreed, so there was no dispute
The island name alone caused the battle
A supply exchange removed all disagreement
hard: Which report identifies both a cause and a limit?
Demands and refusal help explain the conflict; they do not make an attack justified
The date alone explains all decisions
A battle result proves every earlier demand was accepted
An invented speech is enough to establish all motives

label: Local conditions
quiz: How did shallow water and coral affect the approach?
They kept boats from coming close to the beach
They allowed boats to sail straight onto the beach
They established every person's exact position
They made human decisions irrelevant
retry: Which explanation uses the shoreline evidence carefully?
Conditions constrained the landing alongside decisions and the defenders' actions
Having ships guaranteed success on land
Coral was the only cause of the battle
A teaching diagram shows every movement exactly
hard: A sketch has no scale but shows boats offshore. Which claim is supported?
It illustrates an approach constraint, not an exact distance
It proves the precise number of metres each person crossed
It identifies the exact location of every defender
It establishes every participant's private plan

label: Outcome and later history
quiz: What was the immediate outcome at Mactan on 27 April 1521?
The defenders defeated the attacking party and Magellan died
Every expedition member completed the world voyage that day
A modern Philippine republic was established
All later voyages to the islands stopped permanently
retry: Why should Mactan's victory be separated from later events?
Survivors and later expeditions continued after the battle
Magellan led voyages after his death
Every later colonial attempt ended that day
No event occurred after 1521
hard: A display says the victory ended all future colonial efforts. How should it be revised?
State the local victory, then distinguish later voyages and colonial attempts
Keep the claim because a victory always ends all future conflict
Replace the date with the date of a modern republic

label: Evidence and remembrance
quiz: What should a learner say about a picture showing a personal duel?

The picture proves the exact actions of both leaders
Every artistic image is an eyewitness record
A dramatic scene proves its dialogue is authentic
retry: How can a report honor Lapulapu without inventing details?

State an exact age without a source
Quote a fictional classroom speech as original
Credit one person and remove all other defenders
hard: Pigafetta did not identify Lapulapu among the fighters. What conclusion is careful?
That detail remains uncertain; neither a personal duel nor absence follows from it
This proves a personal duel occurred
